content:
# Tasks Document

Fourteen tasks. Ordering is load-bearing and each task carries an explicit `_Depends:_` line.

Two principles from the design's Implementation Order shape the decomposition:

- **A boundary that is not a commit boundary is not a task boundary.** `tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*` and `npm run build` runs bare `tsc`, so a partially-applied type change fails the build. Work that must share a commit shares a task number.
- **Guards come before what they guard.** The parity characterization test and the registry lock are early, not late: a parity test written after the changes can only record what the code then does and cannot fail, and per-worktree identity is what creates the registration race the lock prevents.

---

- [ ] 1. Build the unit-level git fixture
  - Files: src/core/__tests__/helpers/git-fixture.ts (new)
  - Create a real repository in a temp directory with linked worktrees in **sibling** and **nested** layouts, plus helpers for a submodule, a bare repo, `--separate-git-dir`, and a symlinked root; tear down on exit
  - Pass `-c protocol.file.allow=always` when adding the submodule
  - Purpose: Give every later task a real repository to test against instead of hand-rolling one twice
  - _Depends: none — this is first_
  - _Leverage: e2e/helpers/worktree-harness.ts (existing repo construction, as reference only — that harness is e2e and stays)_
  - _Requirements: 7.1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Create a unit-level git fixture helper per requirement 7.1. | Restrictions: `git submodule add` from a local path has failed by default since git 2.38.1 (CVE-2022-39253) unless `-c protocol.file.allow=always` is passed — without it the submodule case silently never runs, and that case is the reason the design refuses to reuse the normalization at git-utils.ts:60-66. Do NOT put real-repository tests in src/core/__tests__/git-utils.test.ts: it mocks child_process wholesale at :11-13 and cannot host them without restructuring; give them their own file. Tear down every temp directory. | _Leverage: e2e/helpers/worktree-harness.ts as reference | _Requirements: 7.1 | Success: The fixture builds sibling and nested worktree layouts, a submodule, a bare repo, a --separate-git-dir repo and a symlinked root; all are removed on teardown; the submodule case actually creates a submodule on a clean CI machine. Set this task to [-] in tasks.md before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 2. Write the non-worktree parity characterization test
  - Files: src/__tests__/parity-baseline.test.ts (new)
  - Capture **today's** values for a project with no path argument: the resolved workspace and workflow roots, the file set reaching the diff and the typecheck, containment decisions, `tsconfigPath`, and `projectId`
  - Purpose: Give the existing single-checkout user base a guard that can actually fail
  - _Depends: 1_
  - _Leverage: task 1's fixture, src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts (existing prepare harness)_
  - _Requirements: 3.11, 7.8_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Write a characterization test capturing today's parity observables for a non-worktree project with no path argument, per requirements 3.11 and 7.8. | Restrictions: This MUST be written and passing BEFORE any behaviour change lands. Written afterwards it can only assert what the code then does and cannot detect a regression — which is the whole point, since this population is the one an earlier draft of the design silently regressed by dropping the git-toplevel fallback. Assert each observable individually rather than a single snapshot blob, so a failure names what moved. Do not modify production code in this task. | _Leverage: task 1's fixture, existing prepare test harness | _Requirements: 3.11, 7.8 | Success: Every observable named in requirement 3.11 is asserted individually against current behaviour; the suite passes on the unmodified tree; a deliberate local change to the resolution fallback makes it fail. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 3. Add git resolution primitives with a scrubbed environment
  - Files: src/core/git-utils.ts, src/core/__tests__/git-resolution.test.ts (new)
  - Add `gitCommonDirAbsolute` (`realpath(resolve(cwd, raw))`, no parent-stripping), `gitTopLevel` (null when the command fails), `sameRepository` (false when either side is null), `normalizeIdentityPath`
  - Delete `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` from the env of **every** git call in the module, including `resolveGitRoot`, `resolveGitWorkspaceRoot` and `isGitWorktree`
  - Resolve `SPEC_WORKFLOW_SHARED_ROOT` to an absolute path in `resolveGitRoot`
  - Purpose: Give inference a same-repository test an inherited environment cannot subvert
  - _Depends: 1_
  - _Leverage: task 1's fixture, existing GIT_EXEC_OPTIONS and try/catch fallbacks in git-utils.ts_
  - _Requirements: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 2.9, 7.4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add the four resolution helpers to src/core/git-utils.ts with a scrubbed git environment, per requirements 1.4-1.7, 1.9, 2.9 and 7.4. | Restrictions: Do NOT reuse the normalization at git-utils.ts:60-66 — it strips .git and returns the repository root, which makes a submodule compare equal to its superproject and makes a filesystem join land on a nonexistent path. Compare common directories directly, never a derived parent. sameRepository must return false when either side is null, or two non-git directories compare equal and inference fires between them. Scrub every git call in the module including isGitWorktree, which has no production callers today and is a trap the moment one is added. normalizeIdentityPath needs stated behaviour, a stated fallback when realpath fails, and its own tests — it is used for identity hashing in a later task. | _Leverage: task 1's fixture | _Requirements: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 2.9, 7.4 | Success: All ten layouts from requirement 7.4 are covered; a symlinked root compares equal to its own linked worktree; a superproject and submodule compare unequal; with GIT_DIR exported to an unrelated repository two unrelated paths compare unequal; two non-git directories compare unequal; gitTopLevel returns null in a bare repo and inside .git; normalizeIdentityPath is unit-tested including its failure fallback. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 4. Add the registry lock
  - Files: src/core/registry-lock.ts (new), src/core/project-registry.ts, src/core/__tests__/registry-lock.test.ts (new)
  - `withRegistryLock` acquiring via `fs.open(lockPath, 'wx')` after ensuring the directory exists, releasing in `finally`, retrying within a bounded time budget, and on exhaustion logging prominently and continuing unregistered
  - Distinguish `EEXIST` (contention, retry) from every other errno (report, do not spin); judge staleness from the lock file's `mtime`; break atomically by renaming aside and proceeding only if the rename succeeded
  - Use a per-process unique temp filename for the registry write; wrap `registerProject`
  - Purpose: Close the lost-registration race **before** the change that creates it
  - _Depends: none (touches only project-registry.ts and a new module)_
  - _Leverage: src/core/project-registry.ts:147-157, :187-226_
  - _Requirements: 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add an exclusive lock around registerProject's read-modify-write, per requirements 6.1-6.6. | Restrictions: ensureRegistryDir is called only from readRegistry:87 and writeRegistry:148 — both INSIDE registerProject, i.e. inside the critical section — so on a first run the global directory does not exist and fs.open(lockPath,'wx') fails with ENOENT, not EEXIST. That is exactly requirement 6.2's scenario. Create the directory before acquiring, and classify errnos: EEXIST means contention, anything else means report rather than spin. Do NOT use isProcessAlive for staleness: it returns true unconditionally when both path-translation variables are set, making a crashed container's lock permanently unbreakable. Do NOT judge staleness from a self-reported timestamp; use fs.stat mtime. Breaking must be atomic — stat-then-unlink-then-open races and two processes can both acquire. Do NOT throw on exhaustion: registerProject is awaited before the transport connects, so throwing kills the MCP handshake. Scope to registerProject only. | _Leverage: src/core/project-registry.ts:147-157, :187-226 | _Requirements: 6.1-6.6 | Success: N concurrent registrations against a nonexistent registry file AND a nonexistent global directory produce N entries; two contending stale-lock breakers do not both acquire; budget exhaustion logs and continues; the temp filename is unique per process. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 5. Resolve both roots and register the inference flag
  - Files: src/core/git-utils.ts, src/index.ts, src/server.ts, src/__tests__/index-args.test.ts
  - Implement `resolveWorkspaceRoots` with the precedence chain `SPEC_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE` (skipped in dashboard mode) → `--no-workspace-inference` → inference → `resolveGitWorkspaceRoot(configuredPath)`, gating inference on `sameRepository` **and** a successful `gitTopLevel` on both sides
  - Validate the environment override with `stat().isDirectory()`, falling through to inference on failure and warning on a different-repository value
  - Validate an **inferred** workspace inside `initialize`, falling back to the configured path with a log rather than throwing
  - Register `--no-workspace-inference` at all five parse sites and reject `--flag=value` boolean forms with an error naming the bare form
  - Replace the log block at :218-225 with one emission reconciled across both conditions
  - Purpose: One decision point for identity, with a usable off-switch shipped in the same commit that turns inference on
  - _Depends: 3, and must not land before 2 or 4_
  - _Leverage: task 3's helpers, src/core/path-utils.ts (validateProjectPath), src/index.ts:180-181_
  - _Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.8, 1.14-1.18, 2.1-2.11_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add resolveWorkspaceRoots, wire it into parseArguments, validate inferred paths in initialize, and register the inference flag, per requirements 1.1-1.3, 1.8, 1.14-1.18 and 2.1-2.11. | Restrictions: The flag registration and the resolver MUST land together: this is the commit that turns inference on for every user, and the validation loop at index.ts:116-128 throws Unknown option for any flag absent from validFlags — so shipping the resolver first leaves the documented escape hatch causing a startup failure. validateProjectPath is async (path-utils.ts:280) and both resolveWorkspaceRoots and parseArguments are synchronous, so the inferred-path check goes in initialize where the predicate is already awaited at server.ts:66 — and must fall back with a log, not throw. The fallback MUST be resolveGitWorkspaceRoot(configuredPath), not the raw configured path. Do NOT merely fix the =value filter: the boolean reads are exact-string matches, so a stripped --no-workspace-inference=true would be read as false, silently discarding the opt-out; reject it instead. index-args.test.ts declares a vi.mock factory with exactly two git-utils exports — an incomplete factory throws every test in the file — and its three call-graph assertions must be re-derived. | _Leverage: task 3's helpers, validateProjectPath | _Requirements: 1.1-1.3, 1.8, 1.14-1.18, 2.1-2.11 | Success: The full precedence matrix is tested; the fallback returns the git toplevel; inference does not fire when either toplevel lookup fails; an inferred path failing validation falls back with a log; a non-directory env value falls through and a different-repository value warns; the flag works in bare form and is rejected in =value form along with the other two booleans; --help lists it; task 2's parity test still passes. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 6. Make ToolContext.workspacePath required and split both runner contracts
  - Files: src/types.ts, src/server.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts, src/dashboard/multi-server.ts, plus sixteen test sites across ten files
  - Add the required field; annotate the literal at src/server.ts:95-99; change `setupHandlers(context: any)` to `context: ToolContext`
  - Split `TaskReviewRunner.RunOptions` into `workflowRoot` and `workspacePath`; keep `AdversarialRunner.RunOptions` single-field and pass the workflow root to its private spawn helper as an argument
  - Wire all six route sites: `:1791`, `:1853` (both roots), `:828`, `:969` (workflow root to the handler), `:852`, `:1012` (workspace to the runner)
  - Purpose: Land the contract and its first real consumer together, so nothing is built on a placeholder
  - _Depends: 5_
  - _Leverage: src/server.ts:61, the compiler as the enumeration mechanism_
  - _Requirements: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 5.1-5.8_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Make ToolContext.workspacePath required, update every construction site, and split both runner contracts with all six route sites, per requirements 3.1-3.4 and 5.1-5.8. | Restrictions: INDIVISIBLE — tsconfig.json includes src/**/* and the build runs bare tsc, so any intermediate state fails the build. Adding the field alone produces 19 errors with server.ts NOT among them, because setupHandlers(context: any) launders the unannotated literal; both the annotation and the parameter type are required. Do NOT silence fixtures with `{} as ToolContext` — an assertion compiles and passes undefined at runtime. Run tsc to enumerate sites rather than working from a list. The runner split is in the same task deliberately: without it, task-review-runner.ts:100 has only the workflow root to supply, so the field would carry a value its type contract denies while later tasks build on it. There are FOUR adversarial call sites, not two — the retry route at :969 and :1012 reproduces both defects, and the obvious mechanical fix at :969 (workspacePath: project.originalProjectPath) preserves the bug; the handler sites need the workflow root because adversarialReviewHandler immediately calls getWorkflowRoot on what it receives. AdversarialRunner must NOT gain a second RunOptions field; its spawn helper takes the workflow root as a parameter so requirement 2.13's env can be set. | _Leverage: src/server.ts:61 | _Requirements: 3.1-3.4, 5.1-5.8 | Success: tsc is clean; server.ts:96 was among the pre-fix errors; no fixture uses a type assertion; getSpecPath resolves against the workflow root and spawn cwd is the workspace on both runners; an adversarial review and a retry both locate their target document from a worktree. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 7. Scrub GIT_* from code-path git invocations
  - Files: src/core/task-diff.ts, src/core/typecheck.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts
  - Delete the four `GIT_*` variables from `runGit`'s env (task-diff.ts:23-27), the typecheck spawn env (:153), and both agent spawn envs (:368, :147), setting the two `SPEC_WORKFLOW_*` roots explicitly at the spawn sites and preserving the path-translation prefixes
  - Purpose: Stop an inherited environment silently making git read another repository
  - _Depends: 6 (the spawn sites need the roots the runner split provides)_
  - _Leverage: src/core/task-diff.ts:23-27_
  - _Requirements: 2.12, 2.13_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Scrub the four GIT_* variables from the three code-path git invocation sites and set the SPEC_WORKFLOW_* roots explicitly at both spawns, per requirements 2.12 and 2.13. | Restrictions: runGit at task-diff.ts:23-27 sets env to a spread of process.env plus GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS — it inherits wholesale and scrubs nothing, and it runs in the PARENT process so neither spawn-site scrub reaches it. With GIT_DIR pointing elsewhere, git diff --numstat returns empty stdout at EXIT 0, so runGit reports ok:true, computeTaskDiff takes the success path with no rejection, and the reviewing agent is told the changes were already committed. Preserve SPEC_WORKFLOW_HOST_PATH_PREFIX and SPEC_WORKFLOW_CONTAINER_PATH_PREFIX — the child needs them for path translation. | _Leverage: src/core/task-diff.ts:23-27 | _Requirements: 2.12, 2.13 | Success: With GIT_DIR exported to an unrelated repository the diff is still correct; the four variables are absent from both child envs; the two SPEC_WORKFLOW_* roots are present and correct in both. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 8. Move safeRealpath into core and implement the file resolver
  - Files: src/core/file-resolution.ts (new), src/tools/review-task.ts, src/core/__tests__/file-resolution.test.ts (new), src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts
  - Move `safeRealpath`, its `warnOnce` set and `_resetValidateWarnings` into core, changing the return to expose the errno while keeping the warn policy unchanged
  - Implement `resolveLoggedFiles`: anchor relative entries workspace-then-workflow-root, classify absolute entries by containment only, mark ambiguous only for relative entries anchoring under both, count the six drop causes, drop rather than substitute on the ENOENT-then-workflow-success case, dedupe by realpath, and enforce containment via `validatePathWithinBases` with both bases realpath-normalized
  - Purpose: Resolve logged paths against the right tree and report honestly what could not be resolved
  - _Depends: 1_
  - _Leverage: task 1's fixture, src/core/path-utils.ts (validatePathWithinBases), src/dashboard/approval-storage.ts:204-239 (existing workspace-first ordering)_
  - _Requirements: 4.8-4.18_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Move safeRealpath into src/core/file-resolution.ts with an errno-exposing return, and implement resolveLoggedFiles, per requirements 4.8-4.18. | Restrictions: safeRealpath and the resolver must land together — the resolver cannot distinguish ENOENT from EACCES without the return change, so requirements 4.13 and 4.14 are unimplementable while it is unchanged. Keep the warn policy exactly: silent on ENOENT, warnOnce on every other code; its committed test block including the ELOOP message assertion moves with it. Anchoring and classification are DIFFERENT operations — path.resolve ignores its base for absolute inputs, so a single resolve-against-each-root function is a no-op for absolute entries and marks every one ambiguous. validatePathWithinBases THROWS a fixed message rather than returning a boolean, so wrap each entry and emit the reviewer-facing warning from the resolver, not the primitive. Both containment bases must be realpath-normalized since resolved paths are. Never accept the workflow root itself: in a nested layout it contains every sibling worktree. Dedupe by realpath is load-bearing once the pre-resolution is deleted, because the existing new Set dedupes raw strings and `src/foo.ts` vs `./src/foo.ts` survive it. A core module must not import from src/tools/. | _Leverage: task 1's fixture, validatePathWithinBases | _Requirements: 4.8-4.18 | Success: A bare relative path resolves to the workspace; absolute paths under each root are classified correctly and asserted NOT ambiguous; a relative path anchoring under both is ambiguous; all six drop causes are counted separately; a file deleted in the workspace but present in the workflow root is dropped, not substituted; ENOENT drops emit no warning; two spellings of one path appear once; containment accepts .spec-workflow above the workspace and rejects a sibling worktree in a nested layout, including under a symlinked workflow root. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 9. Wire the resolver into handlePrepare and carry the labelled list to the prompt
  - Files: src/tools/review-task.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts
  - Delete the `.map(p => path.resolve(projectPath, p))` at :360-361, keeping the `new Set` at :360; pass raw log entries to the resolver
  - Route `workspaceFiles` to the diff, the typecheck and the hygiene signals; keep spec, steering, settings and workflow-root reads shared
  - Convert `buildPrompt`'s eleven positional parameters to an options object and change `filesToReview` to the labelled shape, updating `:277` and the two committed assertions
  - Purpose: Make code operations read the worktree, with the file list reaching the agent intact
  - _Depends: 6, 8_
  - _Leverage: task 8's resolveLoggedFiles, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:110, :212, :277_
  - _Requirements: 4.1, 4.7, 4.21, 4.24, 4.25, 4.26_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Delete the path pre-resolution, wire resolveLoggedFiles into handlePrepare, and carry the labelled file list through buildPrompt, per requirements 4.1, 4.7, 4.21 and 4.24-4.26. | Restrictions: The deletion and the labelled-shape change must land together with buildPrompt. The deletion must NOT land after the two-root partition — deleting the .map alone is safe because the resolver re-anchors against the workflow root, matching today, but the reverse order resolves every relative entry against the wrong tree and then drops it on containment. Convert buildPrompt's eleven positional parameters to an options object FIRST: inserting a field into that list silently shifts methodology into the new slot, outputPath into methodology, and the real output path into priorReviewContext — all assignable, so tsc reports nothing and the agent never learns where to write its result. The destructure at :110 is any-typed, so the compiler catches none of the shape change. Keep the new Set at :360. Decide and state what containment rejection warns, since the current message names projectPath and there are now two roots. | _Leverage: task 8's resolver | _Requirements: 4.1, 4.7, 4.21, 4.24-4.26 | Success: Bare relative log entries resolve to the workspace; .spec-workflow entries reach the labelled file list but not the diff, typecheck or hygiene inputs; spec, steering and settings still read from the workflow root; the rendered prompt shows each file with its root and no object placeholders; a dashboard-triggered review is inspected to confirm; all migrated assertions pass. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 10. Split the typecheck root and key the incremental cache per workspace
  - Files: src/core/typecheck.ts, src/tools/review-task.ts, src/core/__tests__/typecheck.test.ts
  - Add a **required** second root parameter: workspace for `tsconfigPath` (:113), `resolveTscBinary` (:134), the `-p` argument (:146) and `spawnTsc`'s cwd (:153); workflow root for the cache directory mkdir (:139-140) and `ensureGitignoreEntry` (:141)
  - Key the `tsbuildinfo` filename per workspace; make `unwrapTypecheck` (review-task.ts:391) report `tsconfigPath` from the workspace
  - Update the twenty-five existing call sites in the test file
  - Purpose: Typecheck the worktree without creating `.spec-workflow` in it, dirtying its tracked `.gitignore`, or sharing one incremental cache across worktrees
  - _Depends: 9_
  - _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts:113, :134, :139-146, :153_
  - _Requirements: 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Give runProjectTypecheck a required second root parameter and key the incremental cache per workspace, per requirements 4.2-4.6. | Restrictions: There are FIVE root uses that determine which tree is compiled, not three — tsconfigPath, resolveTscBinary, the -p argument at :146, spawnTsc's cwd at :153, and unwrapTypecheck's reported tsconfigPath. Missing -p or the spawn cwd compiles the main checkout while reporting the worktree's tsconfigPath, which is a path that lies about which tree was compiled. The cache DIRECTORY goes on the workflow root but the cache FILE must be keyed per workspace: a single tsc.tsbuildinfo written with --incremental against different -p roots by every worktree is at best a full rebuild every run and at worst concurrently truncated, tripping TSBUILDINFO_REBUILD_RE on unrelated reviews. The second parameter must be REQUIRED: an optional one compiles while leaving the default silently on one root, which an equal-roots parity test cannot detect. src/core/__tests__/typecheck.test.ts has twenty-five call sites passing a single root and is compiled by the bare-tsc build. | _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts:113-153 | _Requirements: 4.2-4.6 | Success: A typecheck in a worktree compiles that worktree — verified by asserting on the compiled file list, not just tsconfigPath; no .spec-workflow appears in the worktree; only the workflow root's .gitignore is touched; two worktrees do not share a tsbuildinfo; tsconfigPath is identical across success, unavailable and rejection arms; all twenty-five call sites updated; task 2's parity test still passes. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 11. Add the actionable file-resolution disclosure
  - Files: src/tools/review-task.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts
  - Add `fileResolution: { workspaceCount, workflowCount, drops }` to the prepare response and carry it through the runner into the prompt
  - When `workspaceCount === 0` and the task logged files, **replace** the "Read every file listed" instruction (task-review-runner.ts:281) and the `nextSteps` guidance (review-task.ts:426) with a statement that no reviewable files were resolved and that a pass must not be returned on that basis
  - Purpose: Stop an all-drop review producing a confident verdict over nothing
  - _Depends: 9_
  - _Leverage: src/tools/review-task.ts:410-426, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:110, :281_
  - _Requirements: 4.19, 4.20_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add the file-resolution disclosure and make the all-drop case actionable, per requirements 4.19 and 4.20. | Restrictions: A note added above an unchanged "Read every file listed" instruction does NOT satisfy requirement 4.20 — the agent still receives an empty list, an instruction to read it, and R4_2A_DIFF_EMPTY's fabricated claim that the changes were already committed, which is the passing-verdict-over-unexamined-code harm the requirement names. Both the prompt instruction and the nextSteps must be replaced on the all-drop path. The runner destructures five fields from an any-typed prepareResponse.data at :110 and discards the rest, so the field must be added there too or it never reaches a dashboard-spawned reviewer, with no compiler error. Keep this minimal — counts and the replacement text, not the structured execution-context object, which belongs to worktree-review-signals. | _Leverage: src/tools/review-task.ts:410-426, task-review-runner.ts:110, :281 | _Requirements: 4.19, 4.20 | Success: An all-drop prepare returns counts and the replacement guidance; both appear in the prompt built for a dashboard-triggered review and in the direct-call response; the read-every-file instruction is absent on that path; a review run against an all-drop task does not return a pass. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 12. Assert diff containment and surface the rejection
  - Files: src/core/task-diff.ts, src/tools/review-task.ts
  - Assert every diff pathspec is contained by the workspace before invoking git; on failure set `TaskDiffResult.rejection` with text stating a containment failure rather than an unexpected exception
  - Purpose: Stop a mis-partitioned pathspec discarding the whole diff and reading as "already committed"
  - _Depends: 9_
  - _Leverage: src/core/task-diff.ts:9 (existing rejection field, consumed at review-task.ts:101-102)_
  - _Requirements: 4.22, 4.23_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Assert diff pathspec containment before invoking git and surface a rejection on failure, per requirements 4.22 and 4.23. | Restrictions: Reuse the existing TaskDiffResult.rejection field at task-diff.ts:9 — it is already consumed at review-task.ts:101-102 — rather than adding a second field. Do NOT detect the out-of-tree case by matching git's stderr: the message is gettext-marked and translates, so a localized git falls through to the benign classification.
